chunks.arabic_text: وَعَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى، عَن أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَن عَلِيٍّ بْنِ رِيَابٍ، عَن أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ الْحَذَّاءِ، عَن أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: And from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riab, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: مَنْ أَفْتَى النَّاسَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلَا هُدًى لَعَنَتْهُ مَلَائِكَةُ الرَّحْمَةِ وَمَلَائِكَةُ الْعَذَابِ، وَلَحِقَهُ وَزْرُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِفَتْيَاهُ

translations.en: Whoever gives fatwa to the people without knowledge or true guidance, the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment curse him, and the burden of the one who acts by his fatwa attaches to him.

en.summary: This hadith outlines the spiritual and ethical consequences for those who issue religious rulings (fatwa) without sufficient knowledge and guidance. It states that such individuals are cursed by both the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment, and they bear the weight of the deeds performed by those who follow their rulings.
en.seo_question: What are the consequences of giving fatwa without knowledge in Shia Islam?
